authoredVerbs._what: Every verb a research file wrote in an edge's `type` (or `rel`) that is not one of the twelve types, mapped explicitly to one of them. The edge keeps the verb as `authoredVerb` for phase 7. A verb not in this map is a REJECT in merge.py, never a coercion. `swap: true` turns the edge round so that `a` is the actor the type expects.

denied-by.why: 'X denied-by Y' names the denier on `b`; the denial type expects the denier on `a`. It joins the unadjudicated list until data/denial-adjudication.json carries a verdict for it.

instrument.why: moved from the plan's default (legislative): its one edge is aawsap -> aawsap-contract-hhm402-08-c-0072, labelled 'prime contract'. A contract is money, which is what `funding` means ('who paid, contracted or was paid').

structural.why: moved from the plan's default (programmatic): its one edge is uapda-sec-9010-eminent-domain -> uapda-2023, labelled 'section of'. Both ends are legislation and the relation is a statute and its own section, which is what `legislative` covers; nothing ran or produced anything.

predicateRules._what: Redesign phase 7 (notes/plans/P7-relationship-vocabulary.md). A predicate refines an edge: it says in a controlled verb what the edge's sentence says, and which end it reads from. research/_predicates.json carries one per edge id; build_app_data.py joins it onto each node's connections and onto edges.json. Predicates are presentation and navigation only: they never change a type, a tier or a source.
predicateRules.classes: `subject` and `object` list the node classes a predicate allows at each end; "any" allows all eight. A domain node (class `domain`) is allowed at either end of every predicate: the 58 domain nodes are topic nodes, absorbed by topics in phase 5, and stand for whatever their topic is about.
predicateRules.denial: Where data/denial-adjudication.json names a denier for an edge, a predicate of the `denial` family on that edge must have the denier as its subject.
predicateRules.display: The page groups connections by FAMILY, the reliable unit (random-sample disagreement 14.9% at family level against 21.2% at predicate level; notes/plans/P7-classification-record.md). A predicate's own label, and its direction, are shown only where its confidence is high; otherwise the row reads the family's `phrase`, which has no direction. The edge's authored sentence is shown on every row either way.
predicateRules.fallback: connected_to is for an edge whose sentence supports no predicate here. It refines no type, and verify.py holds it to at most 3% of edges.
predicateRules.refines: Every predicate names the one edge type it refines. An edge may carry a predicate that refines another type when its sentence plainly says so; the edge's own type is never changed by that, and the crossings are listed in notes/plans/P7-classification-record.md for phase R.
predicateRules.subject: `subject` in research/_predicates.json is `a` or `b`: the end the forward label reads from. Read from the other end, the inverse label applies.
predicateRules.symmetric: A symmetric predicate reads the same from either end (forward equals inverse); its subject is recorded as `a`.
